stem: The Indian Constitution comprises of-
expl: The Indian Constitution has more than 470 Articles; however, many of these are connected to the original Articles as sub-clauses such as (a), (b), (c), etc. In the original text of the Constitution, there were 22 Parts, 395 Articles and 8 Schedules. Through amendments, some new Articles were added and some Articles were also deleted. New Schedules were also added, and their number increased from 8 to 12.

stem: Untouchability is abolished by which Article of the Indian Constitution?
expl: Untouchability has been abolished by Article 17 of the Constitution. This Article states that “untouchability” is abolished and its practice in any form is forbidden. The enforcement of any disability arising out of “untouchability” shall be an offence punishable in accordance with law.

stem: Which Article of the Constitution gives precedence to Constitutional provisions over the laws made by the Union Parliament/State legislatures?
expl: Article 13 provides that the State shall not make any law which takes away or abridges the Fundamental Rights granted in Part III. If any law is made in violation of Fundamental Rights, it shall be void to the extent of such violation. Article 32 relates to the Right to Constitutional Remedies. Article 245 deals with the extent of laws made by Parliament and the Legislatures of States. According to Article 326, elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies shall be on the basis of adult suffrage.

stem: Under which Article(s), the Speaker can allow any member of the House to speak in his/her mother tongue?
expl: According to Article 120 (1) of the Indian Constitution, the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha or the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, or the person acting as such, may permit any member—who cannot adequately express himself/herself in Hindi or English—to address the House in his/her mother tongue.

stem: In which schedule of the Indian Constitution are the formats of 'oath or affirmation' given?
expl: The Third Schedule of the Constitution contains the forms of oath or affirmation. It provides the formats of the oaths/ affirmations to be taken by: Union and State Ministers (oath of office and oath of secrecy); candidates for election to Parliament and State Legislatures; members of Parliament and State Legislatures; judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts; and the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.

stem:
Consider the following subjects belonging to Different lists of the consitution of India Which of the following subjects belong to concurrent list?
1. Protection of wildlife
2. Income on Agriculture
3. Tax on Electricity consumption or sale
4. Price control Out ofthese:
expl: In the Seventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution, legislative subjects are divided into three lists—Union List (List I), State List (List II) and Concurrent List (List III). On subjects included in the Concurrent List, both Parliament and the State Legislatures can make laws; however, if there is a conflict on a Concurrent List subject, the law made by Parliament prevails. • Protection of wild animals and birds—Concurrent List, Entry 17B. • Tax on agricultural income—State List, Entry 46. • Tax on the electricity consumption or sale —State List, Entry 53. • Price control—Concurrent List, Entry 34. Therefore, as per the options, only (1) protection of wildlife and (4) price control come under the Concurrent List.

stem: Which of the following Subject lies in the Concurrent list?
expl: In the Indian Constitution, to strengthen the federal structure, subjects were allocated for the Union and the States and divided into the Union List, State List and Concurrent List. Education was initially included in the State List. However, considering its equal importance for both the Union and the States, it was placed in the Concurrent List by Section 57 of the Constitution (Forty-second Amendment) Act, 1976.

stem: W hich of the following schedules of the Indian Constitution contains provisions for the allocation of seats in the Council of States?
expl: The Fourth Schedule of the Indian Constitution mentions the number of members/seats allocated in the Rajya Sabha for States and Union Territories. The Indian Constitution is divided into 22 Parts and, as per counting, it contains more than 470 Articles and 12 Schedules.

stem: The Fifth Schedule deals with the governance and protection of the interests of which specific group of people?
expl: The Fifth Schedule relates to the governance and protection of interests of Scheduled Tribes. Under the Fifth Schedule of the Indian Constitution, provisions have been made regarding the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes. Under these provisions, it is the duty of the Governor of each State to submit to the President, annually or whenever required by the President, a report regarding the administration of Scheduled Areas in that State.

stem: Which one of the following Schedule of the Constitution of India contains provisions regarding Anti-defection Act?
expl: In the Indian Constitution, by the 52nd Constitutional Amendment (1985), provisions relating to disqualification on the ground of defection were inserted under the Tenth Schedule. It contains provisions regarding defection by a whole group, split within a group, and voting contrary to the direction of an authorised person of the party. Through this, for the first time in India, political parties were given constitutional recognition.
